sections.title: Basic Config — every setting
sections.summary: Screen-level behaviour: entrance animations, cached media, a device-permission prompt, and auto-advance. This guide documents every setting of the Basic Config block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Basic Config section
sections.summary: Behavior settings for this screen that do not change its visible copy: the entry animation, preferring cached assets, requesting a system permission, and an optional auto-advance countdown. Most screens can be left at their defaults — reach for these only for timed intros or permission prompts.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: HeroContent, ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, TextInput, WheelPicker, HeroList, WebEmbed, Paywall.

sections.title: Play Screen Animations
sections.summary: Turns on the entrance, exit, and element animations you set up in the screen's animation settings; when off, the screen simply appears instantly. Use it on intro and hero screens where motion feels polished and guides the eye. Leave it off on dense question screens where visitors want the controls ready to tap right away.

sections.title: Auto-Advance Duration
sections.summary: The number of seconds or minutes (unit chosen below) before the screen moves on by itself, from 1 to 300. Only used when auto-advance is on. Keep it short, about 2 to 4 seconds for a splash or 'analyzing...' screen, so visitors aren't left waiting and bouncing.

sections.title: Auto-Advance After A Delay
sections.summary: When on, the screen moves to the next step on its own after the countdown you set below, with a visible timer. Off by default. Great for splash or 'analyzing...' screens, but never use it where visitors must tap or answer, like questions or your paywall, or you'll skip them past the response or sale.

sections.title: Seconds Or Minutes
sections.summary: Sets whether the auto-advance duration above counts in seconds or minutes. Only shows when auto-advance is on. Seconds is the right choice for nearly every onboarding screen; minutes is rarely useful and risks visitors leaving before the screen ever advances.

sections.title: Reuse cached media
sections.summary: When on, the screen reuses media it has already cached instead of re-downloading it, which can speed up loading for visitors on slow or flaky connections. Leave it off by default for standard web ad funnels, since there's nothing to reuse until assets are cached. Turn it on only if you ship pre-bundled assets or expect a lot of poor-connectivity traffic.

sections.title: Which Permission To Ask For
sections.summary: Picks which device permission this screen requests: push notifications, ad tracking (needed for accurate ad attribution on iPhones), or location. Only shows when the permission request is turned on. Choose what your funnel truly needs, ad tracking if you rely on ad-network attribution, notifications for re-engaging users later.

sections.title: Ask For A Device Permission
sections.summary: When on, this screen pops the phone's own permission request, notifications, location, or ad tracking, chosen in the field below, as it appears. This fires in the native app SDK, not on a plain web page. Put it on a screen that first explains why you need it so far more people tap Allow.
